open-question.question: From what are the notes of an extension release composed: the finish summaries of the missions scoped to `gurita-vscode/` since the previous extension release, as `/release-plugin` composes the plugin's notes from finished missions, the commits in between, or text the maintainer writes?
open-question.recommendation: The changelog decision gives every release an entry, which closes the no-notes option; a draft composed from the scoped finish summaries is the composition `/release-plugin` already runs, and the maintainer's revision is what lets the first release, made inside this still-live mission, name the listing work no finished mission records yet.
open-question.alternative: The skill composes a draft from the finish summaries of the missions under `gurita-vscode/` finished since the previous extension release, falling back to the commit range on an empty range, and the maintainer then revises or adds to it, for instance to name the work of a mission still live at release time, before the text is used; the maintainer's revised text is what is published. The routine case costs the maintainer only a review, while work the finished-mission record cannot show, the publishing mission's own listing work on the first release above all, can still be stated in the notes. The notes are no longer reproducible from the record, two runs can publish different text for one version, and the revision step needs a point in the run where the maintainer is present, which depends on the sibling deciding whether the skill pauses before publishing.

The notes are composed by the release skill from the finish summaries of the missions whose directory lies under `gurita-vscode/` and that were finished since the previous extension release, read through `missions.py missions` and `summary` and rewritten into one condensed `###` section per mission, newest finish first, exactly as `/release-plugin`'s step 5 does. An empty range, no extension mission finished since the last release, falls back as `/release-plugin` falls back: one `### Changes since` section condensed from the commits in the range that changed `gurita-vscode/`, released only on the maintainer's explicit yes. The maintainer writes no text of the notes. It reuses a composition the project already runs and trusts, from a record every extension mission already writes through `/finish-mission`, so the notes cost nothing extra to produce, match the plugin's release-note shape, and a version-only rebuild still has a path that never takes itself silently. Only finished missions count, so work released before its mission finishes is missing: the first publication, made by the skill inside this still-live mission, would list the three finished extension missions but none of this mission's own listing work. Its "since the previous release" boundary and its same-day check need an extension release marker and an earlier-notes record to read, which depend on the siblings owning the extension's tag and changelog.

The notes are composed from the same source as the first option, the finish summaries of the missions under `gurita-vscode/` finished since the previous extension release, condensed into one section per mission. An empty range is a stop: the skill prints that no extension mission was finished since the last release and publishes nothing, so every extension release is backed by at least one finished mission. The maintainer writes no text and the commit range is never read. Every release's notes come from the one condensed record the workflow already produces, with no second path and no confirmation to describe or test, so a release can never go out with notes rebuilt from task-level commit subjects. A release with no finished mission behind it, such as a rebuild to bundle a newly released plugin's missions tool or fixed lines, or a fix made by hand, cannot be published without first defining and finishing a mission for it. It shares the first option's dependence on an extension release marker for the boundary and its blindness to the publishing mission's own work.

The notes are composed from finish summaries as in the first option, but the mission set is every mission finished since the previous extension release that changed what the package carries, whatever its scope: the missions under `gurita-vscode/` and also root-scoped plugin missions that changed a bundled source (`core/tools/missions.py`, `docs/skill-reference.md`, `VERSION`) or a path under `gurita-vscode/`. Each kept summary is condensed into a section that keeps only what a user of the extension would notice. An empty range falls back to the commit range with the maintainer's explicit yes, as in the first option. The notes follow the package rather than the mission's placement, so a plugin release whose missions tool or fixed lines a package bundles, which changes what the extension shows, is reported in the extension's notes instead of passing unmentioned. The selection is no longer one scope query: the skill must join missions to the paths their task commits changed and to the bundled files, and a root-scoped mission's summary describes plugin changes the rewrite must cut down to their effect on the extension, a judgment the scoped options never make. How far plugin changes reach a package also depends on the sibling deciding from which repository state a release may be built.

The notes are composed from the commits between the previous extension release and `HEAD` that changed a path under `gurita-vscode/` or a bundled source, their subjects and, where a subject is not self-explanatory, their bodies, condensed into one bulleted section of user-facing changes. Mission summaries are not read and the maintainer writes no text. It needs no finished mission, so it reports everything the package actually received, the publishing mission's own unfinished work and hand commits included, and it works the same on the first release as on every later one. Most commits in the range are `Task-completion:`, review, annotation, and answer commits whose subjects are task-level or process detail, so the skill must condense hundreds of them (364 commits have changed `gurita-vscode/` so far) into user-facing notes, a larger and less repeatable judgment than condensing a few mission summaries already written for that purpose. The range's start depends on the sibling owning the extension's release marker.

The notes are text the maintainer writes for each release, given to the skill as its input or typed when the skill asks for it, and published verbatim; the skill composes nothing from missions or commits. The maintainer says exactly what a listing reader should know, including changes no mission summary or commit subject names well, and the skill carries no composition logic to write, test, or keep in step with `/release-plugin`'s. Every release costs the maintainer writing and recalling what changed, with nothing checking the text against what was released, and the skill can never run unattended, which constrains the sibling deciding whether it pauses for confirmation.

An extension release carries no notes of its own: nothing is composed or written, and the listings show the version and the README alone, the record of what changed staying in the repository's mission and commit history. The skill has no composition step at all, and no text exists that can drift from the history or differ between the two registries. A user updating from a listing has no way to see what a version changed without reading the repository's history. It is coherent only if the release writes notes nowhere, which depends on the siblings deciding whether the extension gets a changelog and whether a release creates a GitHub release.

open-question.question: `/release-plugin` composes the plugin's release notes from every mission finished since the last tag, whatever its scope, so the next plugin release would list the missions scoped to `gurita-vscode/`. Do those missions stay in the plugin's release notes, or does `/release-plugin` leave them out once the extension has releases of its own?
open-question.recommendation: The plugin's notes then describe only what a plugin user receives, by a mechanical test on the path field the skill already reads, and no extension mission goes unrecorded, because the extension's first notes take up every one finished before it.
open-question.alternative: `/release-plugin`'s step 5 drops every finished mission whose path lies under `gurita-vscode/`, from the next plugin release on, the three extension missions already finished after `2.0.0` included; a mission scoped elsewhere, the root included, stays in the plugin's notes even when it changed the extension. The test is the path field `missions .` already prints, so no new query is needed. The plugin's notes describe only what the plugin's users receive, through a one-line, mechanical filter on a field the skill already reads, with no cutoff date or tag to track. The three missions finished before the extension has a release of its own appear in no plugin notes, so they are recorded publicly only if the extension's notes take them up, which turns on how the sibling question on the release notes source settles; a root-scoped mission that changes only the extension still lands in the plugin's notes.

`/release-plugin` stays as it is: step 5 keeps every mission `missions.py missions .` lists as finished since the last tag, whatever its scope, so the three extension missions already finished after `2.0.0` and every later mission scoped to `gurita-vscode/` get full sections in the plugin's `CHANGELOG.md` entry and GitHub release, beside the extension's own release notes. This mission changes nothing in the skill, and a later mission may still split the notes. Nothing in `/release-plugin` changes, and the root changelog stays the one complete record of everything finished in the repository, so no mission's record depends on how the extension's own notes are composed. Plugin users, who install from the `gurita-<host>` distribution repositories that carry no extension, read sections about changes their release does not contain, and each extension mission's summary is published twice, once in each product's notes.

`/release-plugin`'s step 5 drops a finished mission whose path lies under `gurita-vscode/` only when it was finished after the extension's first release, so the three extension missions already finished after `2.0.0`, and any finished before that first release, stay as full sections in the next plugin release's notes, and later ones are left to the extension's own notes. Every extension mission gets exactly one public record: those predating the extension's releases in the plugin's notes, the rest in the extension's, with none dropped and none duplicated. The skill needs a cutoff it can read, the extension's first release, which exists only in whatever form the sibling questions on the extension's tag and release commit give it, and the rule keeps a one-off transition branch in `/release-plugin` for good.

`/release-plugin`'s step 5 drops a finished mission whenever every file its task commits changed lies under `gurita-vscode/`, whatever its scope, and keeps any mission that changed a file outside it, the plugin's `core/`, tools, or docs among them; it applies from the next plugin release on, the three already finished extension missions included. The rule follows what each mission actually changed rather than where it was placed, so a root-scoped mission that touched only the extension leaves the plugin's notes and an extension mission that also changed a plugin file stays in them. The skill must read each kept mission's task commits and their file lists, which `missions` and `summary` do not print, adding per-mission history reads and a judgment on mixed missions to a release step that today reads two queries; the three already finished missions' public record depends on the extension's notes source as under the scope rule.

`/release-plugin` keeps every finished mission, but step 5 composes the missions whose path lies under `gurita-vscode/` into one section of their own at the end of the plugin's entry, headed as the VS Code extension's, apart from the plugin's per-mission sections, in full as today. No mission's record is lost whatever the extension's own notes become, while a plugin user can see at a glance which changes are not part of the plugin. The extension's changes are still published in the plugin's changelog and GitHub release and again in the extension's notes, and the skill gains a grouping rule and a second section shape to keep.

`/release-plugin` composes no section for a mission whose path lies under `gurita-vscode/`; in their place the plugin's entry carries one line naming those missions' titles and pointing at where the extension's own notes stand. Plugin readers keep a trace that the extension changed in the same interval without reading its detail, and the detail is published once, in the extension's notes. The line needs a stable target to point at, which exists only if the sibling questions on the extension's changelog and GitHub release give it one, and the three missions already finished are reduced to titles if the extension's notes do not take them up.
